name: Data Table
summary: Everything a table means is in its markup — which cell is a header, and what the whole thing is called. Draw those instead of declaring them and there is nothing left to read: a bold first row is not a header row, and the restyle that stacks the cells onto a phone throws away the column it was trying to save.
demoNote: Every readout here is written by hand and checked against the real accessibility tree by the spec, so it cannot drift. Example 2 puts the stacked-card restyle beside the table it came from; example 3 is the same two columns as plain cells, as column headers, and as both; example 4 is one wide table in two wrappers; example 5 names a table four ways, two of which are not names.
